title: What’s All That Coffee Doing to Your Gut? - Nautilus
gist: University of Copenhagen nutrition scientists used the SmartPill ingestible sensor plus urine and stool analysis to compare gut physiology and microbiota between habitual and infrequent coffee drinkers; the excerpt's subtitle says the effect is good but results aren't detailed.

insights.claim: Coffee's health benefits range from mood-boosting to reducing mortality, but little is known about what habitual coffee drinking does to the gut.
insights.so_what: Gut-health research could support coffee health positioning.

insights.speaker: Jake Currie

insights.claim: University of Copenhagen nutritional scientists sent a SmartPill electronic capsule through the digestive systems of habitual and infrequent coffee drinkers to measure temperature, pH and intestinal contractions, and analyzed urine and stool samples for intake and gut flora.
insights.so_what: Ingestible-sensor diagnostics are being used in nutrition research.
